walkthroughs.body_html:
Practical Skills in Biology — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Practical Skills in Biology brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Practical Skills in Biology.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which scientist proposed 'omnis cellula e cellula' (all cells from pre-existing cells)?
options: Schleiden
Schwann
Virchow
Hooke

mcqs.q: The fluid mosaic model of the cell membrane was proposed in 1972 by:
options: Watson and Crick
Singer and Nicolson
Schleiden and Schwann
Margulis and Lovelock

mcqs.q: Why is interspecific competition between similar species important?
options: PCR uses enzymes from bacteria to cut DNA into fragments, then sticks them back together.
Competition means physically fighting and is rare in nature.
Two species cannot occupy exactly the same niche indefinitely — competition often leads to displacement or niche divergence.
Competition only happens between predators and their prey.

mcqs.q: What are the three repeated stages of one PCR cycle?
options: Denaturation (high temp, strands separate), annealing (lower temp, primers bind), extension (Taq polymerase synthesises new strands).
PCR uses enzymes from bacteria to cut DNA into fragments, then sticks them back together.
PCR has just one stage — heating the DNA until it copies itself.
Competition means physically fighting and is rare in nature.

mcqs.q: What drives water up the xylem in a tall tree?
options: Competition means physically fighting and is rare in nature.
Capillary action alone is enough to lift water to the top of any tree.
Transpiration pull — evaporation from leaves creates tension that pulls water up the continuous water column.
Roots actively pump water up to the leaves like a heart.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Endosymbiotic theory”?
options: Phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins; selectively permeable (Singer & Nicolson 1972).
Mitochondria and chloroplasts originated from free-living prokaryotes engulfed by ancestral eukaryotes (Margulis 1967).
As cells grow, volume increases faster than surface area, limiting diffusion; drives mitotic division.
Cell without membrane-bound nucleus or organelles; DNA in nucleoid; includes bacteria and archaea.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Eukaryote”?
options: Cell with membrane-bound nucleus and organelles; includes protists, fungi, plants, animals.
Mitochondria and chloroplasts originated from free-living prokaryotes engulfed by ancestral eukaryotes (Margulis 1967).
Cell without membrane-bound nucleus or organelles; DNA in nucleoid; includes bacteria and archaea.
As cells grow, volume increases faster than surface area, limiting diffusion; drives mitotic division.

Cell without membrane-bound nucleus or organelles; DNA in nucleoid; includes bacteria and archaea.
Cell with membrane-bound nucleus and organelles; includes protists, fungi, plants, animals.
As cells grow, volume increases faster than surface area, limiting diffusion; drives mitotic division.

Phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins; selectively permeable (Singer & Nicolson 1972).
